clue.text: Stars of use to landsmen

explanation.surface: A star group that farmers find helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation also called the Big Dipper bears this name, and the same word names the farm implement that turns the soil.

clue.text: Do the French take it for granted?

definitions.text: Do the French take it for granted?

parts.words: Do the French take it for granted?
parts.note: to slip away without permission is to take it 'French'; it is also permission itself, something granted

explanation.surface: A wry question about French presumption.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'take French leave' means to go off without asking, so the French are teasingly said to take permission for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is what is granted, and the idiom pairs the word with the French.

clue.text: In which Jane, of strip cartoon fame, often appeared

definitions.text: In which Jane, of strip cartoon fame, often appeared

parts.words: In which Jane, of strip cartoon fame, often appeared
parts.note: Jane, the Daily Mirror wartime strip heroine, kept losing her clothes and was usually seen in her smalls

explanation.surface: A recollection of a famous comic-strip heroine's usual appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane was a British newspaper cartoon strip whose heroine was forever being caught half-dressed; 'strip' hints at undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine was typically drawn in her lingerie, the clothes worn beneath outer garments.

clue.text: A person of sound perception

parts.note: 'sound perception' reads as good judgment but means perceiving sounds, i.e. one who listens

explanation.surface: Praise for someone with good judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is one who perceives sound through the ears.

clue.text: It sounds alarmingly early

parts.note: the rooster's call at dawn works as a natural alarm clock, sounding very early

explanation.surface: A complaint about a noise that goes off too soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is announced by the rooster's call, which wakes people like an alarm.

clue.text: What must be tackled squarely every day

definitions.text: What must be tackled squarely every day

parts.words: What must be tackled squarely every day
parts.note: 'squarely' suggests honestly, but refers to the grid of squares solvers tackle in each day's paper

explanation.surface: Advice to face one's daily task head-on.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily newspaper brainteaser is solved square by square in a grid.

clue.text: There's nothing in ice-creams to go to people's heads!

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for headgear, things worn on heads

indicators.note: the word nothing sits inside the ice-creams, which is how 'in' places one piece within another here

parts.note: cornets are ice-cream cones, so ice-creams in cones
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A warning that ice-cream is not intoxicating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to people's heads' suggests intoxication, but means small crowns worn on heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Small crowns worn by nobles sit on the head, so they literally go on people's heads.

clue.text: An example of that of boat-builders

definitions.text: An example of that of boat-builders

parts.words: An example of that of boat-builders
parts.note: a vessel is an example of a boat, and a trade or skill is what boat-builders practise: one word covers both

explanation.surface: A riddle about the product of a shipyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a vessel and a skilled trade, so a boat exemplifies the boat-builder's skill.

clue.text: No whisper of a change of possession

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A property dispute settled without a whisper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' is the anagram signal; 'of a' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something is having it as one's possession.

clue.text: No sinecure for those with convictions

definitions.text: No sinecure for those with convictions

parts.words: No sinecure for those with convictions
parts.note: 'convictions' suggests firm beliefs but means criminal sentences; a sinecure is an easy job

explanation.surface: A remark that principled people never get easy jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: A sinecure is a paid post needing little work; convicts used to be sentenced to strenuous prison toil.
explanation.definitionFit: The old prison sentence of toil was the very opposite of an easy post.

clue.text: River among a number in Italy

definitions.text: River among a number in Italy

parts.words: River among a number in Italy
parts.note: one of Italy's many rivers, the one that flows through Florence and Pisa

explanation.surface: A geography note on Italian waterways.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tuscan waterway runs through Florence and is one of many Italian rivers.

clue.text: Incomparable, the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A boast that the lower chamber has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commons is the chamber with no lords in it: peer-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal means matchless; the Commons is literally without members of the nobility.

clue.text: Official version of a try-on

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An attempt to fool an official.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'try-on' is British slang for a cheeky attempt to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: A public functionary who certifies documents is a kind of legal official.

clue.text: It was passed unanimously at former peace conferences

definitions.text: It was passed unanimously at former peace conferences

parts.words: It was passed unanimously at former peace conferences
parts.note: 'passed' suggests a resolution voted through, but means a smoking implement handed round by Native American negotiators

explanation.surface: A report on a resolution approved at peace talks.
explanation.definitionFit: The calumet, a ceremonial tobacco smoker, was handed round all present at peace talks.

clue.text: This man is not to be seen among the characters in Wells

definitions.text: This man is not to be seen among the characters in Wells

parts.words: This man is not to be seen among the characters in Wells
parts.note: H. G. Wells wrote a novel about a scientist no one can see; the clue says he cannot be seen

explanation.surface: A remark about a figure absent from a cast list.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells's title character cannot be seen, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Direct confirmation of successful appeal

explanation.surface: A plain statement that an appeal has succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders appeal 'How's that?'; an umpire who agrees gives the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means downright or direct; split, it is the umpire agreeing a batsman is dismissed.

clue.text: One who is dull, or amusing, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words might be arranged otherwise, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A judgment on whether someone is boring or entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant, slow-witted person is a dunce, one who is dull of mind.

clue.text: A tumble-down affair all up in the wood

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word all is read upwards, back to front

explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble-down' suggests a shack, but means a fall; in a down clue 'up' reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling down or caving in is a tumble.

clue.text: Bowler's burden — it's the last straw!

definitions.text: Bowler's burden — it's the last straw!

parts.words: Bowler's burden — it's the last straw!
parts.note: a bowler bowls an over, his burden; the last straw is what makes a load too heavy

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler at the end of his tether.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers a set of six balls called an over; the final straw breaks the camel's back by making its load excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive burden is too much weight, the final straw that breaks the camel's back.

clue.text: Knocking back these small drinks shows what your head will do

parts.note: after too much drink your head will spin

explanation.surface: A warning about the effect of downing shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Small measures of spirits are drams or tots.

clue.text: A trying number

parts.note: 'trying' suggests troublesome, but means trying a case: the size of a jury

explanation.surface: A tiresome quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury of a dozen people tries a case, so it is the trying count.

clue.text: She is to meet The Third Man

parts.note: after Adam and Cain, Abel was the third man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman due to meet the hero of a famous film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Third Man' is a film, but here the third man of the Bible after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name stands for any woman, she.

clue.text: Just the one for a dog-fight?

definitions.text: Just the one for a dog-fight?

parts.words: Just the one for a dog-fight?
parts.note: one breed of dog shares its name with a prizefighter, ideal for a fight

clue.text: At one time it may have helped a man to keep his head

parts.note: 'keep his head' suggests staying calm, but means escaping beheading by a stay of execution

clue.text: Island in the spring

explanation.surface: An island visited in springtime.
